story: On Wednesday evening at 8:17 in Sumter Oaks, the air is mild at 78 degrees under partly cloudy skies. Gary, grateful as ever, settles in at Rosa's house while she looks over his sketches for the speaker mount and lights, both agreed to be removable and kept within quiet hours. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna, gracious but a little flustered, promises Hal she'll set aside extras so they reach three before nine tomorrow, and Hal, gruff but warm, announces he's coming along to make sure the sketch stays within code.

gary.thought_process: Rosa's penciling in Thursday to walk my sketches to the review desk, which is a real kindness since she's juggling per-diem shifts. I've already spread out the clamp list and sketched the string-light layout, so no point fussing over it again. Best thing I can do is thank her, confirm the sketches are labeled and ready, and say I'll have the clamp list and light plan tucked in the folder tonight so she doesn't have to wait on me. Then I can get to work on her cart.

parameters.content: Thursday works fine by me, Rosa, and I appreciate you carrying those sketches over. Everything's labeled, and I'll tuck the clamp list and your light layout in the folder tonight so you can just grab it and go.

donna.thought_process: Hal just told me he's counting my flamingos and taking his tally to the committee at nine tomorrow. I already asked him about Rosa's cart sketch, and he didn't answer that part, so I shouldn't repeat the invitation. Better to respond to what he actually said. I want to stay on good terms and not get into a fight on the street. The honest thing is to check what's actually visible from the street. I'll thank him for the heads-up, say I'll look at the flock myself tonight and tuck any extras out of sight before the committee meets, and keep it friendly since he'll be at Rosa's table anyway.

parameters.content: Well, I appreciate you telling me to my face, Hal, that's what a good neighbor does. I'll go through the flock tonight and tuck any extras around back so we're at three before nine tomorrow.

hal.thought_process: Donna asked if I'm headed to Rosa's to help sketch the parade cart. I've already told her my piece about the flamingos and the committee, so no sense repeating it. The parade cart is Gary's, and I do want to see what he's building before I file anything on L-01. Besides, I'll admit I'd like to show up for them. Rosa's house is connected from here. I'll answer her plainly and head over.

parameters.content: I'll come along, Donna. Somebody ought to keep the sketch within the code, and I'd like to see this cart before the committee does. Lead the way.

rosa.thought_process: Gary's at my table sketching string-light layout and a speaker mount. I've already penciled in Thursday's free hour for the review desk, so no need to re-ask. The one thing worth saying now is the legal side: L-01 says exterior cart mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, and L-03 means no amplified sound after 10 PM. I want us honest with Review, so I should ask Gary to make the mount removable and keep the speaker plan within quiet hours. That moves things forward without repeating myself.

parameters.content: Those sketches look great, Gary. Let's put the speaker mount and lights on the review form exactly as you drew them, tuck-on and removable, and I'll keep the music off before 10 PM so we're clean on quiet hours.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
